plants.name: Osmanthus fragrans
plants.description: An evergreen shrub or small tree bearing clusters of tiny, intensely fragrant flowers with a scent reminiscent of ripe apricots and peaches. Widely cultivated in gardens and temple grounds across East Asia.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (September to October in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to China and Japan; cultivated in East Asia, the southern United States, and Mediterranean climates
plants.funFact: Osmanthus blossoms are used to flavor teas, cakes, jams, and liqueurs, and the Mid-Autumn Festival in China is traditionally associated with its fragrance.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up goblet-shaped flowers in autumn without any leaves present, which emerge the following spring. Often found in damp meadows and woodland edges.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to mid autumn (September to October)
plants.location: Europe, from the British Isles to central Europe; widely naturalized in gardens elsewhere
plants.funFact: It is nicknamed 'naked ladies' because the flowers appear without foliage, and it is the source of colchicine, a compound used in medicine and plant breeding but highly toxic.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A spectacular tropical and subtropical tree that blankets itself in trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers before its fern-like leaves fully emerge. Streets and parks turn purple during its peak bloom.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to November)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in South Africa (Pretoria), Australia, and Argentina
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, there are tens of thousands of jacarandas, earning it the nickname 'Jacaranda City,' and fallen blossoms create purple carpets on the streets.

plants.name: Symphyotrichum novae-angliae
plants.description: A tall, robust native perennial wildflower with daisy-like flower heads featuring golden centers. It provides vital late-season nectar for pollinators, especially migrating monarch butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, in meadows, prairies, and roadsides
plants.funFact: Monarch butterflies rely heavily on New England asters as a nectar source during their autumn migration to Mexico.
